bullets.title: Fed hawks warn rates too low; inflation path to 2% requires more restriction
bullets.body: Dallas Fed's Logan stated inflation is not sustainably returning to 2% on its current path and that modestly higher rates would better balance risks—one month of lower CPI is insufficient evidence. Separately, Kansas City Fed's Schmid called inflation 'persistent across a broad range of goods and services' and pushed back on treating price rises as transitory shocks. Both officials noted the labor market is well-balanced or strengthening, removing the argument for imminent cuts.

bullets.title: Fed's Logan: AI investment surge risks nonlinear inflation; data centers add to power demand pressure
bullets.body: Logan flagged that the AI investment boom could trigger nonlinear price increases, with demand effects already present while productivity benefits may take years to materialize. She also noted data-center electricity demand will add modest inflationary pressure, and that U.S. oil export growth is being driven by inventory drawdowns rather than new production, constraining supply response despite elevated prices.

bullets.title: July Philly Fed Manufacturing surges to 41.4 vs. 12.5 estimate—highest since Nov 2021
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Fed Business Outlook jumped to +41.4 in July against consensus of +12.5 and prior reading of +10.3, with new orders at +37, shipments +33.7, employment +10, and prices paid edging to +53.9. The broad beat signals strong regional manufacturing momentum, though rising prices paid adds to inflation concerns flagged by Fed speakers.

bullets.title: Jobless claims beat at 208K; labor market resilience intact
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 208K for the week—a 2-month low—versus 217K consensus and 216K prior. Continuing claims also came in below estimates at 1.805M vs. 1.818M expected. The data reinforces the Fed hawks' view that the labor market is not deteriorating and provides no cover for near-term rate cuts.

bullets.title: Retail sales in-line at +0.2% but ex-auto and control group decelerate sequentially
bullets.body: June retail sales met the +0.2% m/m consensus, with the prior month revised up to +1.0%. However, ex-autos and gas slipped to +0.4% vs. +0.8% prior, and the control group decelerated to +0.5% vs. +0.8%—suggesting consumer momentum is cooling at the margin even as headline spending holds up. Motor vehicles/parts +1.9% and e-commerce +1.9% were bright spots; gas stations -5.3%.

bullets.title: Housing data deteriorates sharply: pending home sales -5.4% vs. -0.5% estimate; NAHB misses
bullets.body: June pending home sales collapsed 5.4% month-over-month versus -0.5% consensus and +3.5% prior—a significant miss signaling housing demand weakness. The July NAHB Housing Market Index also disappointed at 34 vs. 35 estimate and prior 36, with single-family sales and buyer traffic both declining. The 30-year mortgage rate hit 6.55%, its highest since August 2025, compounding affordability pressure; mortgage applications fell 2.7% week-over-week.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector under pressure: SMH down 5%, breaking below May highs; Nasdaq-SOX divergence flagged
bullets.body: The semiconductor index fell another 5% to break below its initial May highs, though it remains up ~53% year-to-date. The prior session saw the rare combination of Nasdaq +0.5% while SOX fell 2%+—a historically unusual divergence since 2010. Multiple large-cap semis moved below their 50-day moving averages, though NVDA has been the notable outperformer. Goldman also cut its global PC shipment forecast citing a memory chip crunch derailing the upgrade cycle.

bullets.title: South Korean market turmoil: 1-in-30 retail investors margin-called, regulator suspends leveraged ETFs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs reported over 1.2 million leveraged Korean retail accounts triggered margin calls as of July 13, with 320K–360K accounts fully liquidated. Korean stock market volatility now exceeds levels seen during the GFC and the 1997–98 Asian financial crisis. The regulator suspended new single-stock leveraged ETF listings and raised margin requirements. Goldman advises clients to rotate out of Korea and into the Chinese AI value chain.

bullets.title: US-Iran military conflict escalates: strikes near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm; Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb closure risks rise
bullets.body: Iranian media reported U.S. missile strikes near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island—the fifth consecutive day of U.S. strikes. Iran warned of 'infrastructure for infrastructure' retaliation and declared Strait of Hormuz control an 'unbreakable red line.' The White House confirmed a full Hormuz blockade is in force and reported Iran struck U.S. bases in Kuwait and Jordan. Separately, Iran reportedly instructed Houthis to prepare Bab el-Mandeb closure if the U.S. targets Iranian power infrastructure.

bullets.title: Oil near $85/bbl; diesel hits $5/gallon nationally—inflation risk building in supply chain
bullets.body: Brent crude recovered from ~$70 at the start of the month to $85/bbl before dipping back slightly; the White House cited U.S. actions for a 'stable oil market' but geopolitical risk remains elevated. National average diesel prices crossed $5/gallon per GasBuddy, threatening to reverse recent inflation relief across consumer goods including food and lumber. U.S. natural gas storage declined sharply to 41B cu ft vs. 61B prior week.

bullets.title: Gold falls below $4,000/oz; silver crashes 54% from ATH and hits 7.5-month low
bullets.body: Spot gold broke below $4,000/oz (last -2% at $3,981) as safe-haven positioning unwound. Silver simultaneously crashed to its lowest level in 7.5 months, down approximately 54% from all-time highs, with high retail participation in the position. Wells Fargo upgraded commodities to 'Favorable' from Neutral in the same session.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2: 25% revenue growth to $39.9B; raises FY guidance; stock sells off on 'triple play'
bullets.body: TSMC reported its fourth consecutive 'triple play' (beating revenue, operating, and net income) with Q2 revenue up ~25% YoY to $39.9B from $31.9B. The company raised both full-year revenue and capex guidance and cited the AI cycle's expansion from accelerators to full-stack infrastructure. Revenue mix: 66% HPC, 22% smartphone, 12% other. Despite strong results and 67.7% gross margin, shares traded lower in a familiar beat-and-decline pattern.

bullets.title: Nvidia CEO: 'We are at the beginning of the AI cycle'; Japan building national AI factory with 27,500 Rubin GPUs
bullets.body: Jensen Huang, speaking in Tokyo, stated the AI boom is still in its early stages. Separately, Japan announced it is building the world's first national AI factory featuring 27,500 Nvidia Rubin GPUs, 13,750 Vera CPUs, and 140 MW of data center capacity. Nvidia remains the clearest positive public-market read-through for AI infrastructure, with the Thinking Machines Inkling model requiring GB300/NVL72 multi-GPU configurations.

bullets.title: EU orders Google to open Android and Search to rivals; structural remedy imposed
bullets.body: The EU issued a formal order requiring Google to open its Android platform and Search capabilities to competitors, following antitrust findings on dominance in search and AI markets. The mandate is structural and enforceable. Separately, Google is rebranding NotebookLM as Gemini Notebook and expanding its Gemini app with personalized avatar features, and announced an Intel partnership to deploy Gemini Enterprise across Intel's enterprise operations.

bullets.title: Mag 7 diverges from semiconductors: GOOGL and MSFT lead premarket while NVDA lags
bullets.body: Premarket moves showed Alphabet +1.3%, Microsoft +1.3%, Amazon +0.7%, Apple +0.4%, Meta +0.3%, Tesla -0.2%, and Nvidia -1.5%, illustrating a clear Mag 7 vs. semiconductor rotation. Goldman traders characterized the AI market as a 'rubber band' stretched to breaking point, and market observers noted Mag 7 is rising while SOX falls with CAPEX cut announcements anticipated.

bullets.title: BofA fund manager survey at most bullish since post-pandemic inflation surge; stock-bond ratio at YTD high
bullets.body: BofA's global fund manager survey shows sentiment at its most optimistic since the post-pandemic inflation peak, with the majority expecting neither a soft nor hard landing. Separately, a risk-matched stock-to-bond relative performance ratio hit its highest year-to-date level, implying elevated market expectations for economic growth—even as semi stocks and housing data point to pockets of weakness.

bullets.title: Consumer spending growth unsustainable: 7% nominal spend vs. 3% income growth; debt collector lawsuits surge
bullets.body: One analyst noted that consumer nominal spending running at ~7% against 3% income growth is historically extreme and has never persisted more than a couple of quarters without stimulus support. Separately, lawsuits filed by debt collectors over unpaid credit card bills surged to their highest levels in years, corroborating emerging consumer credit stress beneath the headline spending data.

bullets.title: US slaps 25% tariffs on Brazil; Brazil rejects action and denies legal basis
bullets.body: The U.S. imposed 25% tariffs on Brazil after Rubio cited failed negotiations with the socialist government. Brazil formally rejected the Section 301 investigation, stating there is no legal justification, and noted it has held 30+ contacts with U.S. officials seeking a negotiated solution. China's exports to Germany have meanwhile surged to 70% above the 2010–2019 trend, signaling ongoing trade-flow distortions globally.

bullets.title: Netflix heads into Q2 earnings with bearish sentiment; four straight negative post-earnings reactions
bullets.body: Market positioning is bearish ahead of Netflix's Q2 2026 report tonight, with engagement headwinds cited as the primary concern. The stock has fallen following each of the last four earnings reports—down 9.7% after April's print and 5.1% a year ago—creating a low-bar setup.

bullets.title: S&P upgrades SoftBank outlook to Stable on ARM stock appreciation; ARM remains credit catalyst
bullets.body: S&P Global revised SoftBank's credit outlook from negative to stable, specifically citing the rise in ARM's stock price as a key credit positive while affirming the BB+ rating. This reinforces ARM's strategic importance to SoftBank's balance sheet and highlights the stock's macro significance beyond pure semiconductor fundamentals.
